\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بوند} (būṅd)}{بوند (būṅd)}]{\ur{بوند} (būṅd) — a drop}

\label{lesson:UR-C428-bund}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a handkerchief, then the Urdu for to look good (on someone).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بوند}}
\textbf{\ur{بوند}} — \emph{būṅd} — \textquotedblleft{}a drop\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بارش} \ur{کی} \ur{پہلی} \ur{بوند} \ur{میرے} \ur{ہاتھ} \ur{پر} \ur{گری۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bārish kī pehlī būṅd mere hāth par girī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The first drop of rain fell on my hand.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بوند}} (\emph{būṅd}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{bū̃d}, \textquotedblleft{}a drop\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{bindú}, \textquotedblleft{}a drop, a spot\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9240).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{būṅd}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{būṅd}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bārish kī pehlī būṅd mere hāth par girī.} — The first drop of rain fell on my hand.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a handkerchief, then the Urdu for to look good (on someone), then say \emph{būṅd} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{بوند} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A drop\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{برسنا} (barasnā)}{برسنا (barasnā)}]{\ur{برسنا} (barasnā) — to pour (of rain)}

\label{lesson:UR-C428-barasna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to look good (on someone), then the Urdu for a drop.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{برسنا}}
\textbf{\ur{برسنا}} — \emph{barasnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to pour (of rain)\textquotedblright{}.

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{بادل} \ur{رات} \ur{بھر} \ur{برسا}, \emph{voh bādal rāt bhar barsā}.

\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a spell of rain, then the Urdu for steam.
